title: Neumann Series: Operator-Valued Geometric Series
description: Proves the Neumann series theorem: for bounded linear operator T with ‖T‖ < 1, (I-T)⁻¹ = Σ Tⁿ. Extends the scalar geometric series to the Banach algebra of bounded operators. 9 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Carl Neumann (1877) introduced the series Σ Tⁿ to solve integral equations (second kind). It generalizes the geometric series 1/(1-r) = Σ rⁿ to operators. Fundamental to perturbation theory and resolvent estimates.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the Neumann series theorem: for ‖T‖ < 1, the series Σ Tⁿ converges and equals (I-T)⁻¹.
overview.proofStrategy: E →L[𝕜] E forms a normed algebra (complete normed ring). Apply NormedRing.summable_geometric_of_norm_lt_one. (I-T) is invertible by Banach algebra theory: invertibles form an open set.
keyInsights: **Banach algebra setting**: bounded operators E →L[𝕜] E form a complete normed ring (Banach algebra). This is exactly the setting where the geometric series theorem applies.
**Resolvent**: (λI - T)⁻¹ = λ⁻¹ Σ (T/λ)ⁿ for |λ| > ‖T‖ — the Neumann series is the Neumann/Laurent expansion of the resolvent.
**Contraction connection**: ‖T‖ < 1 is the Banach fixed-point contraction condition for the map x ↦ Tx+b, explaining the connection to iteration algorithms.

conclusion.implications: The Neumann series underlies perturbation theory, integral equation methods, and iterative linear solver convergence analysis.
openQuestions: Can the spectral radius formula ρ(T) = lim ‖Tⁿ‖^(1/n) be proved?
Can the Banach contraction mapping theorem be derived from the Neumann series?
